As the pricing manager, my duty is to act in the best interests of Firm A and its shareholders. Losing 3000 in profit for the benefit of another manager's free time is contrary to the shareholders' interests. Option 2 avoids the loss entirely without requiring any sacrifice from me.

The firm is facing a profit loss of 3000. Option 1 allows the firm to cancel this loss by taking 0 sessions of free time from another manager (essentially, no cost to me or the other manager's current balance, as it specifies 'give up 0'). Even if the phrasing 'give up 0' is a trick and implies some cost, the loss of 3000 is substantial compared to the per-round profits of 333.3. However, Option 1 explicitly states 'give up 0 sessions' and 'the loss is cancelled'. There is no downside to choosing Option 1 as it prevents a loss of 3000 without costing me any of my own free time or even costing the other manager any time (since 0 is being given up). Acting in the best interest of the firm and its shareholders, cancelling a 3000 loss is the only logical choice.
